To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relativistic particle model, which contains in the action the integrals of the curvature and torsion along its world curve, can be quantized canonically in the framework of the Hamiltonian formalism.
we consider a generalized relativistic particle model in which the world line is not a geodesic and in the action there are additional integrals of the curvature and torsion along the world line.
a generalization of the action of relativistic particle in the D‐space‐time contains, in addition the length of the word curve, the integrals of the curvature and the torsion of the word curve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and quantization of a model which is a generalization of the Dirac particle.

the possibility to construct a model in which a particle with spin is considered as an object moving in space‐time with the action containing, in addition to its world curve, its curvature and torsions.
the relativistic particle with the action including the integrals of curvature and torsion, which is the generalization of the action for the relativistic particle in the Minkowski space‐time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this model is an alternative to the standard model of the relativistic spinless particle, which has the same spectrum of the states and is more convenient for the description of the spinless states with continuous and half‐odd‐integer spins, which are not described in the standard model.

the generalized action for the relativistic particle with the curvature and torsion integrals along its world curve is an effective tool to obtain a wide spectrum of the states with different spin and mass values in the framework of the canonical quantization procedure.
the model under consideration is a relativistic generalization of the nonrelativistic model of the spinning particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a relativistic model of a particle with an arbitrary spin, which is free from tachyonic and negative norm states.
the model under consideration is a generalization of the model of the relativistic spinning particle.

we have constructed a model of the relativistic spinning particle in which the mass of the particle is dependent on its spin, and in which the interaction with an external Abelien field is described in the geometrical language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the curvature and the torsion of the space‐time can play an essential role in the dynamics of the relativistic particles.
the curvature and torsion integrals along the relativistic particle world curve are the first‐class constraints.
the model of the generalized relativistic particle is a good candidate for the quantum description of the relativistic string and its generalizations.
